subject: Banking
title: Insurance at the Point of Sale
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Insurance at the Point of Sale.

hook.text: Buy a flight on Kayak and travel insurance appears at checkout. The entire policy is embedded, purchased in one click.

buildup.text: Traditional insurance requires calling agents, filling forms, and waiting for quotes.

discovery.text: Bolttech and Cover Genius provide APIs that let any retailer sell insurance at checkout without a license.

twist.text: Because the offer appears in the checkout rush, people often buy coverage they barely read or compare.

climax.text: Embedded insurance removes friction but also removes deliberation. Easier access can mean less informed decisions.

punchline.text: One click, instant coverage. Convenience often beats careful analysis.

quiz.question: What drives the growth of embedded insurance?
options: Reduced friction from APIs that add insurance as a one-click option at checkout

details.summary: Embedded insurance integrates coverage into purchase transactions, offering travel insurance at flight checkout, device protection at electronics purchase, or shipping insurance at e-commerce checkout, all powered by bank and fintech partnerships.
details.whyItMatters: Embedding insurance at the moment of purchase captures customers when risk awareness is highest. This model grows the insurance market by making coverage frictionless and contextually relevant rather than a separate chore.
takeaways: Insurance offered at the point of purchase has dramatically higher conversion rates
Banks partner with insurtechs to embed coverage into payment flows
Micro-insurance for single trips or items is now economically viable

faq.question: How does embedded insurance work technically?
faq.answer: When you make a qualifying purchase, the payment platform's API triggers an insurance offer from a partner insurer. If accepted, the premium is added to your transaction. The entire process happens within the existing checkout flow.

faq.question: Is embedded insurance good value for consumers?
faq.answer: Sometimes. The convenience comes at a price. Embedded policies may be more expensive than standalone coverage for the same risk. But for small, specific risks, the ease of purchase often outweighs a minor cost premium.
